result.summary: CODE GATE (2c-i-b): PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. No BLOCKER, no MAJOR. Two MINOR findings and merge conditions on tests (not code defects). Static review only; runtime claims rest on the ELIXIR-DEV report and hosted CI. SCOPE: in scope (mandatory triggers route_scope.ex, scope/enforce.ex, snapshot, plus response.ex and scope_gate.ex as tenant-data response shaping). Verified: (1) THREE FILTER HANDLERS: run_query, run_query_aggregate and run_export call ScopeGate.scope_set at the very top and pass the returned set to Compiler.compile / Compiler.run_aggregate (the three literal :all sites are gone; grep of the diff shows no remaining :all in entities.ex for these routes). Every response is sent on the rebound conn. Cursor.paginate receives the compiled (scoped) query and only AND-s the resume filter onto it; the cursor carries no set and the set is recomputed per request, so page 2 cannot widen. The output has no count/total field (query: items+next_cursor; aggregate: results from the scoped query; export: records+next_cursor+constant metadata). Pre-gate returns are only 400 malformed body (non-2xx, backstop irrelevant); the type-hidden 200-empty envelope is after the gate, so it carries the marker. No error path returns data before the gate. (2) OFF/SHADOW: ScopeGate.mode reads auth_context.scope_enforcement, the same key Authorize.apply_scope_mode uses to call Enforce, so the gate and the backstop agree; not-on returns {conn, :all} / {conn, true} with no query and Compiler :all adds nothing (2c-i-a verified), so bytes are unchanged; the backstop is registered only in the Enforce on branch. (3) MEMO: stored in conn.private (per request process/conn), keyed by permission atom; grants come from the existing per-conn principal memo; nothing global, no ETS, no process dictionary; a different principal or conn cannot see it. The marker is set before the mode test (also under off), harmless. (4) BACKSTOP: registered only for :filter and {:resolver,_} in the on branch; replaces only 2xx without the marker; every non-2xx unchanged; one constant log line scope_not_applied (no ids); rescue and catch inside the callback answer the same detail-free 500 via Response.put_problem(Error.internal()); the exporting handlers use Response.ok (no chunked send) so the body can be replaced. A handler that rebuilds the conn from an older copy loses the marker and gets a false 500 (fail closed, accepted by R-4 e). It cannot be defeated into a LEAK by rebuilding; only by explicitly putting the private key, which is gate-bypass by code review, covered by the ledger and per-route tests. The control remains detective: the marker proves gate called, not result applied. (5) ScopeGate F-1/C-1: guarded/1 rescues ScopeSetError (re-raise, already logged) and any other raise, exit or throw (-> one constant scope_set_failed reason=read_failed line, re-raised as ScopeSetError, mapped by ApiPipeline.handle_errors to the detail-free 500); the {:ok, set} = match inside compute_set is inside guarded, so a bad return also fails closed. Never :all, never partial, never silent :none for a fault. A request with no principal gets :none under on (fail closed). (6) SELF-SERVICE: me.ex, help.ex change is the scope: :self_service declaration only; no handler logic changed. /me/memberships = caller's own data (0051-A7); /me/modules = tenant module metadata (Installs.list_installed, no caller filter); /help/resolved: process_definition_id remains a filter over help rows and stale comes from the selected row's own definition (not from the request id), so it is not a definition-existence oracle; the diff adds no field derived from a scoped resource. Enforce passes :self_service after the coarse allow only. /me and /help each contain exactly these routes plus authz_unmatched. (7) SNAPSHOT: git numstat is 0 added / 6 removed; line count 143 -> 137; the removed lines are exactly POST /entities/query, POST /entities/query/aggregate, POST /entities/records/:entity_type/export, GET /me/memberships, GET /me/modules, GET /help/resolved, no other line touched. (8) WALK: @expected_filter_routes lists the three filter routes and fails both a mounted :filter route not listed and a listed route mounted with another class; @self_service_routes list with rulings 0051-A7, SEC-518-R2-modules, SEC-518-R2-help; new errors :self_service_not_listed (any route under /me or /help not on the list), :self_service_list_mismatch (class differs from the entry, or a :self_service route not on the list), :tenant_wide_unruled, :pending_marker_unlisted are sound for the shipped routes. (9) put_problem/2: send_problem now = put_problem |> send_resp; put_problem does the same effective_trace_id, put_resp_content_type and resp(status, Error.serialise) that send_resp(status, body) did, so denied and error responses are byte-identical (INV-5); put_problem only sets, so a before-send replacement never re-runs the callbacks. (10) NO migration, no secret, no tenant_id column, no new log field beyond two constant lines (INV-1, INV-4, INV-7, INV-10 unchanged; permission_matrix golden not affected, no permission atom or role changed).

findings.title: walk rules omitted by the ELIXIR-DEV deviation leave no expected-list control for a {:resolver, _} declaration
findings.detail: :unexpected_resolver_route, @expected_resolver_routes and :data_route_default were not added. In 2c-i-b no resolver route exists and the omission is acceptable for this slice: Enforce passes a {:resolver,_} route only with the before-send detective check, and a router edit declaring one is not itself a mandatory SECURITY-REVIEWER trigger (routers/*.ex are not on the trigger list), so until the rule exists a mistaken `scope: {:resolver, f}` in a PR would pass the walk.
findings.required_action: 2c-ii MUST add :unexpected_resolver_route with a committed @expected_resolver_routes list (the eight record write and attachment routes) in the SAME change that first declares a {:resolver,_} route, and the :data_route_default rule (design AC 18), each with a seeded walk test. Absence of those in the 2c-ii diff is a FAIL of the 2c-ii gate.

findings.title: walk does not detect a stale or unmounted list entry or a key mismatch
findings.detail: audit_self_service checks mounted routes against the list, but a @self_service_routes entry whose route is not mounted, an entry whose :key differs from the route's policy key, and an @expected_filter_routes line for an unmounted route are not reported. None creates exposure (an entry cannot reclassify a route; the class comes from the route declaration), it only weakens the 'list equals reality' guarantee.
findings.required_action: Optional hardening in 2c-ii or 2d (report unmounted entries and key mismatches). Not required for merge.

conditions_for_merge: Tests T-B1 (fixture filter/resolver route that omits ScopeGate: on gives 500 plus exactly one scope_not_applied line; off/shadow give 200), T-C13 over HTTP (DB fault in the set read gives the detail-free 500 with exactly one scope_set_failed line, never a 200), T-S9 (see R-2), and an on-mode behaviour test per filter route (T-L19.. for query, aggregate, export: a scoped caller sees only in-scope rows, including a second page via next_cursor, a joined query, and export) must exist and pass in CI. The ELIXIR-DEV scratch results do not count as evidence.
T-S4: recorded off/shadow byte-identity rows for the three filter routes (M1, M2, H1 for self-service) captured on main, per the design.
Walk seed tests for :self_service_not_listed, :self_service_list_mismatch, :tenant_wide_unruled, :pending_marker_unlisted and :unexpected_filter_route (both directions) via audit_routes/3.

PR body (AC 23) must carry the table of six reclassified routes below, the six removed snapshot lines, and the R-4 sentence: the before-send check detects a handler that omitted ScopeGate; it does not make a response safe.

A-2: the set is read for requests that later fail validation (2 extra statements under on); no data leaves, acceptable.

A-4 (carry from step-04 A-5): me.ex bare {:ok, memberships} = match is pre-existing, now reachable by scoped users; route to ELIXIR-DEV as a drive-by or issue.
